title: An enum case that reached a `mixed` is judged in a condition by the integer behind it.
text: A case backed by `0` is falsy there, while the same case under its own declared type is truthy, so the two spellings of one value disagree — the one thing `rule:expressions/truthy-table`'s rows are written to prevent. `rule:enums/truthiness` makes every case truthy and `rule:enums/representation` spends no tag on an enum, so by the time [`helpers::value_truthy`] is handed the value there is nothing left to tell it from an `int`; that function's doc says the same from the other side. Closing it means spending the reserved tag, which overturns a rule and is an ADR rather than a slice. What it costs today is a ported `if ($status)` whose enum arrived through an `array<mixed>` or an erased parameter taking the branch PHP never took.
